stem: In the system of equations below, \(k\) is a positive constant. \[y = kx\] \[y = x^{2} + 9\] If the graphs of the two equations intersect at exactly one point, what is the value of \(k\)?
solution: The graphs meet at exactly one point when this quadratic has exactly one solution, so its discriminant is \(0\): \(k^{2} - 36 = 0\).
\(k\) is positive, so \(k = 6\). (The line \(y = 6x\) touches the parabola at \((3, 18)\).)
verify:
x, k = symbols('x k')
ks = [v for v in solve(Eq(discriminant(x**2 - k*x + 9, x), 0), k) if v > 0]
assert ks == [6]
assert len(solve(x**2 - 6*x + 9, x)) == 1
assert [Rational(a) for a in spr_answers] == ks
